ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Michelangelo Buonarroti Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Primary care visit for painful, stiff hands that make writing, drawing, and carving difficult. Concerns: Aching, stiff hands, worst at the base of the left thumb, that make holding a chisel, a pen, or a brush hard; He will not stop carving and wants treatment that keeps him working. [S]

tr.td: Ibuprofen 200 mg oral tablet (over the counter), two tablets by mouth three times daily
Two tablets by mouth three times daily
Allopurinol 100 mg oral tablet, two tablets (200 mg) by mouth daily
Diclofenac sodium 1% topical gel, 2 g to the painful hand joints four times daily, no more than 8 g a day to either hand
Apply 2 g to the affected hand joints four times daily
Acetaminophen 500 mg oral tablet, two tablets by mouth up to three times daily as needed for hand pain, no more than 3 g a day
Two tablets up to three times daily as needed; maximum 6 tablets a day

Radiographs of both hands (posteroanterior, oblique, and lateral): left first carpometacarpal joint-space loss with osteophytes and subluxation (Eaton stage III); narrowing and osteophytes at the left thumb metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints and the left index metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints; osteophytes at the right index and middle distal interphalangeal joints; no erosions, chondrocalcinosis, or hook-like osteophytes
Thumb-base splint fitted: prefabricated hand-based first carpometacarpal orthosis for the left thumb, for heavy work and at night
Injection of the left first carpometacarpal joint with triamcinolone acetonide 10 mg and 1% lidocaine under ultrasound guidance, by rheumatology
Occupational hand therapy: four sessions of joint-protection teaching, thumb-stabilizing and range-of-motion exercises, and tool adaptation for carving and drawing

Irrigation and simple repair of a 2.5 cm laceration of the dorsal left index finger over the proximal phalanx with four 5-0 nylon sutures under a digital block; extensor tendon intact on direct inspection

tr.td: Two acute illnesses, in the summer of 1544 and toward the close of 1545, with recovery; nature not recorded in the cited source
Hand deformities in his later portraits, proposed retrospectively to be osteoarthritis of the left thumb and index finger
Urinary calculus with severe pain, treated with mineral water; passed fragments of the stone and improved; afterwards drank only spring water and changed his way of life
The stone, with difficulty passing water, and pains in the side and back that often kept him from stairs
Writing very troublesome to his hand, eyes, and memory

tr.td: Primary care visit for painful, stiff hands that make writing, drawing, and carving difficult
Four-week hand osteoarthritis review after stopping oral ibuprofen, with rheumatology consultation
Hand osteoarthritis review three months after a thumb-base injection
Hand osteoarthritis and gout review at about seven months
Same-day sick visit for a chisel cut to the left index finger

Hand exercise and joint protection: daily thumb-stabilizing and range-of-motion exercises, padded and thicker tool handles, a lighter mallet, and rest breaks during carving, taught in a course of occupational hand therapy
Hand-based thumb splint for the left first carpometacarpal joint during heavy work and at night

Stop over-the-counter ibuprofen; use topical diclofenac gel first and acetaminophen as needed up to 3 g a day; avoid regular oral NSAIDs at his age because of kidney, blood pressure, bleeding, and gout risks; recheck creatinine in four weeks
Rheumatology consultation to confirm hand osteoarthritis, exclude inflammatory and crystal arthritis, and advise on a thumb-base glucocorticoid injection and further options

CMID osteoarthritis monitoring: pain rating, a validated function measure, grip strength, and joint examination at each visit; ALT when acetaminophen is used regularly; creatinine, blood count, and blood pressure if oral NSAIDs are ever used; no routine repeat radiographs; periodic mood and sleep screening
Continue allopurinol 200 mg daily with serum urate every six months at target; drink at least 2 L of water a day to prevent stones
Falls prevention: platform ladder with a rail, never climbing alone, good studio lighting, and a yearly fall-risk check
Hand pain at or below 3 of 10 on most days by the seven-month review
Carve for at least three hours a morning and write his own letters
Carving three to four hours most mornings; writes short letters with a thick-barrelled pen
No oral NSAID use and creatinine back to his baseline
Ibuprofen stopped; creatinine from 1.21 to 1.02 mg/dL
Serum urate below 6 mg/dL and no gout flare or stone
Urate 5.2 mg/dL; no flare or stone
No falls, with safe ladder and scaffold use
No falls; he uses a platform ladder with a rail and does not climb alone
